subject: quick question regarding var-cov of estimates

messages.author: 4201c816d32af2ef
messages.subject: quick question regarding var-cov of estimates
parts:
Hi.

Hopefully this is a quick question. How might I find out how the
standard deviations of the Phi parameters are calculated (probe
effects). That is, the 'sdPhi' portion of the list when you readUnits
from a ProbeAffinityFile. How are these calculated? Just breezing
through Ben's thesis, it says there are different ways to do it.
Wondering how aroma.affymetrix does it.

Thanks,
Mark

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] quick question regarding var-cov of estimates
parts:
Hi Mark,

the quick answer is that I am indeed not sure exactly which estimate
Ben is using in affyPLM. It is better to check with him directly and
repost here.

He covers some of the standard error estimates in his thesis:

Bolstad, B. M. Low-level Analysis of High-density Oligonucleotide
Array Data: Background, Normalization and Summarization University of
California, Berkeley,

See Section 4, and especially Eqns (4.2)-(4.4), I think.

If you look at the source code of affyPLM, and scan for
'R_wrlm_rma_default_model' and 'R_rlm_rma_default_model', which are
the two native functions aroma.affymetrix is calling. In either case,
you see that the StdErrors are calculated as:

rlm_compute_se_anova(Ymat, rows, cols, beta, residuals, weights,se,
(double *)NULL, &residSE, 4,
PsiFunc(asInteger(PsiCode)),asReal(PsiK));

You find the source for that function in affyPLM/src/rlm_anova.c.

By looking at the code, you should be able to figure out exactly which
estimate he uses.

Cheers

Henrik
